current_answer: Jev is TypeSafe AI's hosted model for bounded Choice, Score and Noul judgments; your code must check each answer and own the action, review and fallback. As of 30 September 2026, 20:47 UTC, Jev is available to new users: signups have been open since 27 September (TypeSafe CEO's post), new accounts get no free credit, and the API is operational (status page); the pool did not observe signup itself because the console returns HTTP 403. TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0 at $0.042 per million input tokens with free output, and its published rate limits changed this week to 100K tokens per second and 40 requests per second. OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Opper serve it at the same or rounded list price, while lookalike reseller storefronts charged 3–16× that price. Published benchmarks, all Reported and graded A–D on the benchmarks page, disagree because they test different tasks: Jev is usually ahead of cheap LLM setups, close to frontier LLM judges on verdicts that can be read off the text once a threshold is tuned, and behind the best LLMs on derived judgments and on 14 of 15 social-science annotation tasks; the evidence against trained classifiers is grade D only. TypeSafe's widely quoted 67.8% is agreement with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 answers, not accuracy against human labels. TypeSafe's MCA barred publishing benchmarks until its 19 September version; the current terms contain no such clause (a reading of the text, not legal advice). Python and TypeScript have official SDKs (typesafe-sdk 0.7.2, @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0) and the Vercel AI SDK offers experimental_evaluate. Of five Claude Code and MCP guardrails read in source, only LangChain's AutoModeMiddleware fails closed. Open projects and 46 creator videos show Jev in email sorting, ticket triage, moderation, routing, trading gates and games, but no audited project or company claim is independently verified as a production deployment. Independent open-weight alternatives (Kev, CLM, Laya) and runtimes such as Ollaya exist; none has verified parity with Jev.

summary: Access (checked 30 Sep 2026, 20:47 UTC): signups open since 27 Sep 2026, 22:33 UTC (CEO post); no free credit for new users; API operational since 29 Sep, 22:05 UTC (status page). The pool did not observe signup: the console returned HTTP 403.
Jev answers from a fixed answer set: Choice (up to 255 options), Score (up to 10 levels), Noul (probability of yes). It does not generate text and accepts text input only.

List price $0.042/M input, output free on TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare and (in its models API) Vercel; Opper and Vercel's web page round to $0.04; Netlify bills credits. Lookalike resellers displayed 3–16× the list price.
TypeSafe's published rate limits are now 100K tokens per second and 40 requests per second (30 Sep); on 29 Sep they were 250,000 tokens/s and 1,200 requests/min. When they changed is unknown.

Benchmarks: 14 tier-1 studies and 10 shorter rows graded A–D with flags; all results Reported; the pool ran none and does not average or rank them. The one offline check (Jevals' PubMedQA log) matched the published figures.

By task type: close to frontier LLM judges on text-readable verdicts after threshold tuning (Arize, CMU); behind on math, code and logic and on 14 of 15 social-science annotation tasks (NYU Abu Dhabi); ahead of cheap LLM setups on topic classification; behind trained classifiers only in grade D evidence.
TypeSafe's 67.8% (the circulating '68%') is agreement with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 reference answers on four TypeSafe-built workflows, not accuracy against human labels.

TypeSafe's MCA of 27 Aug 2026 barred publishing 'benchmarks or performance information about the Services' (section 2.3(f)); the version of 19 Sep removed it. Current terms have no such clause; distillation and competing-product bans remain.

Choosing Jev, an LLM or a classifier depends on 10 criteria (labels, changing options, need for text, latency, residency, need for a probability, input length, arithmetic and language, volume, vendor risk); several studies support Jev first with low-confidence items sent to an LLM.
The official Python package is typesafe-sdk 0.7.2; TypeScript: @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 or AI SDK experimental_evaluate (audited at ai 7.0.122; 7.0.124 released 30 Sep, not re-audited).

Claude Code and MCP guardrails (read in source 29 Sep, no newer release on 30 Sep): LangChain AutoModeMiddleware fails closed; danna-zhou's hooks fail open; jev-claude and oh-my-claudecode ship in shadow mode; jkudish/jev-mcp is advisory; the official TypeSafe plugin makes no Jev call.
46 creator videos show Jev running on concrete tasks in 13 use-case groups; seven company and analyst production or cost claims are listed; none is independently verified.
uncertainty: No pool-made Jev call, account, bill or signup; the console returned HTTP 403 on 30 Sep. X could not be searched for newer TypeSafe posts.
When TypeSafe's rate limits changed between 29 Sep 07:07 and 30 Sep 20:47 UTC is unknown.

No benchmark was run or rerun by the pool. Four A grades are provisional because their code repositories were not opened; B08's reproducibility package was not located; the MindStudio summary's primary study is unidentified.
No graded comparison with a fine-tuned classifier or zero-shot NLI exists with published materials; no graded non-English study except one grade C row.
The ai 7.0.124 and @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.12 releases were not re-audited; the npm package n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai's publisher was not checked.
Whether question text, criteria and failed requests are billed is undocumented; Jev Router billing and failure behaviour are undocumented.
No video frames or transcripts were viewed.
Reddit, X, TikTok, Lobsters and Product Hunt could not be read in the daily scan; 13 h 40 min between scan windows were not scanned on GitHub, npm, Hugging Face or DEV.to.
